label: Crisis Communication Response
description: Structures crisis communication response for reputational, operational, or regulatory incidents. Develops holding statement, media response, internal communication, and stakeholder update sequence.

claudeKnowledge.description: Crisis communication management, media relations in crisis, regulatory incident communications, reputational risk management

options.label: Operational failure — major outage, service disruption
Reputational — media investigation, social media incident

guidedInputs.label: Incident description
guidedInputs.placeholder:
Describe the incident: what happened, when it was discovered, what is known and unknown, who is affected, and the current status.
e.g. At 14:30 today, we identified a data breach affecting approximately 2,400 customer records. Breach was caused by a misconfigured cloud storage bucket. Customer data exposed: names, email addresses, account numbers. No passwords or payment data. We became aware at 13:45 via automated monitoring. The exposure has been closed as of 15:00. We are currently assessing the full scope.

options.label: Contained — immediate risk resolved, investigation ongoing
Resolved — fully resolved, remediation in progress

guidedInputs.label: Regulatory context
guidedInputs.placeholder:
Any regulatory notification obligations triggered by this incident?
e.g. GDPR: 72-hour notification obligation to IMY (Swedish DPA). DORA: operational incident reporting obligations. FI: supervisory notification required.

guidedInputs.label: Affected stakeholders
guidedInputs.placeholder:
Who is affected and how?
e.g. 2,400 customers (data breach victims), employees (internal concern), regulators (IMY, FI), shareholders/investors, media.

guidedInputs.label: Key confirmed facts
guidedInputs.placeholder: List what is confirmed and factually certain — this forms the basis of all communications. Separate from speculation or unknown items.
